newsitem.title: UK: Shell shares at record on merger report.
newsitem.headline: Shell shares at record on merger report.

text.p: Shares in Shell Transport & Trading Co Plc rose in early trading on Monday after a report in the Wall St Journal said Shell Oil and Texaco were in talks on merging their U.S. refining and marketing businesess.
The report said a Saudi company was also involved in the talks which would pool assets valued at more than $10 billion.
Shell shares were up 19p at 10.18 stg by 0729, after initially touching a record 10.22 stg -- surpassing the previous peak of 10.08 stg set October 2.

With crude oil prices firm in Asian trading, British Petroleum shares also rose to be up 14-1/2p at a record 702. On SIMEX Brent futures were offered 20-35 cents above the London close at $24.05 a barrel.
The Wall St Journal report said the merged Shell company would control about 15 percent of the petroleum products market in the United States.
A spokesman for Shell declined comment on the report.

Alan Marshall, an analyst at Robert Fleming, said a U.S. merger involving Shell's refining and marketing activities would be good news if it came off, though potential savings may be less than some may have hoped.
"This is the sort of thing the market should like," Marshall said. "The question is whether it's really going to happen and what it's worth."

"Unlike with BP and Mobil where there was a vast potential for cost cutting, Shell Oil has already been a big turnaround story and one would have thought the scope for cost-cutting would be more limited."
Marshall said it was possible any planned merger could still fall apart if the companies involved took different views of the valuations of the assets involved.

He also pointed out the strong oil price was continuing to boost oil shares. "Crude looks as if it is going to break through to another high today and I guess people are still going to be putting money into the sector," Marshall said.
